title: Burgruine Kropfsberg St. Gertraudi
highlights: Former archiepiscopal frontier bastion at the strategic confluence of the Ziller and Inn rivers
Three monumental keeps enclosed within sweeping 13th-century stone curtain walls
Historically pivotal border control point dividing Tyrolean and Salzburg territories
Scenic circular trail meandering through vineyards and riverine woodlands at the castle's base
kurzbeschreibung: The Burgruine Kropfsberg near St. Gertraudi was a mighty Salzburg border fortress with three preserved defensive keeps.
beschreibung:
Monumental Fortress at the Mouth of the Zillertal

The Burgruine Kropfsberg occupies a commanding strategic position on a wooded hill near St. Gertraudi, right where the Zillertal meets the Inntal. Erected in the early 13th century by the archbishops of Salzburg, the extensive defensive complex served to protect the border against the Grafen von Tirol.

Three Keeps and Historic Walls

Remarkable is the ensemble of three massive keeps that soar above the expansive curtain wall. The ruin stands as a fascinating testament to medieval military architecture and invites walkers on a journey back to the era of the prince-bishops.
